clues: This town sits on the east shore of a big isle in the far east of its land.
The sea holds back the seasons in this place. February, not January, is the coldest month, and August, not July, is the warmest month.
This town was founded by the British in 1785, and it grew into a full city in 1904.
In both world wars, this town was a key stop for ship convoys bound for England. The ships gathered here, then crossed the wide sea in groups.
This town and four near towns form one coast zone. For long, folk have called it the trade coast of its isle.
